newsitem.title: USA: CBOT July soybeans sharply lower on fund sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT July soybeans sharply lower on fund sales.

text.p: CBOT July soybean futures fell sharply in early trade Wednesday on commodity fund selling, floor traders said.
Near the open, Lind-Waldock sold 2.5 million July, Refco sold two million bushels July and one million November and R.J. O'Brien sold one million July, pit sources said.
Local traders were also active sellers in the July contract early, traders said.
Most in the trade had expected soybeans to open higher following a sharply higher close in nearby contracts on Tuesday.
July's inability to puncture resistance seen at $8.55 was also said to prompt technical selling, traders said.
Concern about the effects of the El Nino weather pattern on world grain and oilseed production should lend support to futures, traders said.
At 0950 CDT, July soybeans were 12-1/4 cent per bushel lower at $8.40-1/2 and other months were 1/4 to six cents lower.
